channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Inoreader publishes a live ranking of the web's most-followed news feeds
item.description: Inoreader now publishes a weekly ranking of 50 news feeds based on what its readers actually follow. The October 19 list puts The New York Times first with 141,000 readers, followed by Google News, The Independent and Quartz, offering a useful snapshot of news consumption through RSS.

item.title: A practical OPML guide explains why subscription lists remain portable
item.description: A hands-on guide distinguishes OPML subscription lists from RSS feeds and explains common import failures, including bare ampersands, missing feed addresses and empty outlines. Its key advice is timeless: export your OPML before leaving a reader so a shutdown or lost login cannot take your subscriptions with it.

item.title: CJR connects platform accountability to journalism's democratic role
item.description: Columbia Journalism Review compares years of platform resistance to scrutiny with a federal government that locks out reporters and investigates news networks. Jem Bartholomew argues that independent journalism remains essential because powerful institutions increasingly treat accountability as optional.

item.title: Brewster Kahle argues that the web's memory must survive
item.description: The Internet Archive founder says publishers blocking the Wayback Machine to deter commercial scraping will instead erase evidence used by journalists, researchers and courts. He argues that preservation can coexist with rate limits and safeguards against abusive bulk extraction.

item.title: Slate's 1996 homepage offers lessons for the 2026 web
item.description: A 30th-anniversary revival of Slate's original homepage made its editors appreciate sparse layouts, mixed subject matter, direct traffic and text-first presentation. The exercise is influencing a redesign, with one modern constraint the old site never faced: adapting the simplicity to phones.

item.title: Urgent PHP fixes trigger a global website security scramble
item.description: PHP released fixes for critical flaws already being exploited, prompting government sites and other services to go offline while operators patched. The language underpins WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento; security agencies urged immediate updates, while about 1.5 million visible hosts reported versions with no fix.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 enters beta with a Secrets API and faster media handling
item.description: WordPress 7.2 Beta 1 adds responsive design controls, browser-side image processing, easier navigation management and a standard API for securely storing credentials. It also brings notes onto the editor canvas and adds an “On This Day” widget. The final release is scheduled for December 8.

item.title: Privacy Badger reaches Safari on the Mac
item.description: EFF's free tracker-blocking extension is now available for Safari 26.5 and newer on macOS, giving it coverage across every major desktop browser. Privacy Badger blocks trackers rather than merely limiting their data access, replaces tracking widgets with click-to-activate panels and sends the Global Privacy Control signal.

item.title: Kagan says Supreme Court rulings have damaged American democracy
item.description: Justice Elena Kagan says the court's conservative majority has encouraged a partisan redistricting “race to the bottom” and underestimated the real-world effects of election-law decisions. She also called the surge of money following a June campaign-finance ruling a corruption risk and a nightmare for voters.

item.title: WTF finds a human-made way to give an old podcast new life
item.description: Marc Maron's closed WTF show has republished its 2011 Norm Macdonald interview as a two-hour visual presentation on YouTube. The production adds photographs and contextual material without pretending to animate the conversation, offering a thoughtful model for making valuable audio archives newly discoverable.

item.title: FCC urged to reject synthetic-voice political robocalls
item.description: Senate leader Chuck Schumer asked the FCC to deny a petition that would allow prerecorded political calls using synthetic voices without prior express consent. The agency says it has no plans to grant the request; public-interest groups warn the change would weaken a key defense against deceptive election messages.

item.title: U.S. orders DeepSeek removed from civilian agency systems
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security ordered civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services that use them from their systems. The directive also blocks new acquisitions, citing risks involving data transfer to China, malicious code and software vulnerabilities.

item.title: Britain puts Microsoft’s software bundling under scrutiny
item.description: Britain’s competition regulator proposed giving Microsoft strategic market status, opening the door to rules on bundling, licensing and customer switching. The review will ask whether organizations can combine Microsoft products with alternatives and whether cloud users face barriers to moving providers.

item.title: Publishers join Google licensing program as referral traffic falls
item.description: CNN, Axios, the Financial Times and other publishers joined a Google program that pays for expanded content rights. Google says its generated features will attribute and link to sources, while news organizations seek compensation and ways to counter declining search referrals.

item.title: Sharks lose late lead in Detroit shootout
item.description: San Jose led 3-1 in the third period but fell 4-3 after Detroit tied the game with 1:33 left and won the shootout. Macklin Celebrini had a goal and two assists for the Sharks, who slipped to 1-2-1 over their past four games.
